comparator.name: Bachelor Civil Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's official programme and student portal, checked 2026-09-29, describe the three-year Dutch-language Bachelor Civiele Techniek and its construction, water and transport domains. The latest publicly linked official bachelor regulations provide a complete 2025-2026 curriculum: 60 EC in year one, 60 EC in year two, and 60 EC in year three. The genuine 30-EC minor and the three-course 12-EC specialization choice are preserved without inventing a student choice. The specialization block is represented as one documented choice component because any three listed 4-EC specialization courses satisfy it.

components.name: Minor
components.note: Genuine open minor space preserved from the official curriculum.

components.name: Three specialization courses
components.note: Choose three 4-EC courses from the official list spanning structures, water, roads, underground space, climate impacts and integrated infrastructure design.

programmes.label: Bachelor Civil Engineering at Delft University of Technology

exception.reason: TU Delft's Civil Engineering bachelor is built around a cumulative engineering spine: three structural-mechanics courses, construction materials, concrete and steel structures, soil mechanics, fluid mechanics, hydrology, hydraulic engineering, surveying, road and railway design, foundation design, dynamics and two large Bouwplaats project courses. UCR offers strong environmental, delta, water, earth-science and spatial-planning content plus useful mathematics, but it does not offer the structural, materials, geotechnical, hydraulic, transport or construction-engineering sequence on which the degree's integrated projects depend. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be an environmental-sustainability or delta-studies programme with quantitative tools, not Civil Engineering.
exception.curriculumContext: The latest publicly linked official TU Delft regulations account for the complete 180 EC: 60 EC of compulsory first-year mathematics, mechanics, materials, water, transport and design; 60 EC of compulsory second-year mathematics, mechanics, structures, soil, fluids, hydrology and engineering design; and a 60-EC third year comprising a genuine 30-EC minor, a 10-EC bachelor project, Surveying and Mapping (4 EC), Road and Railway Design (4 EC), and three 4-EC specialization courses selected from an official list. Programme learning outcomes require application of mechanics of structures, fluids and soil, hydrology, materials and transport to civil and environmental structures and infrastructure.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. ENSDELT111 Building with Nature and ENSDELT211 Living with Water directly address ecosystem-based flood protection, resilient infrastructure and delta water management; ENSENVI212 Soils & Aquifers, ENSENVI211 Earth Observation, ENSENVI112 Natural Hazards, Risks & Adaptations and ENSSUST313 Research in a Sustainable Delta add soil and groundwater fieldwork, GIS, hazards and applied sustainability research. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics supply useful quantitative tools. The workbook nevertheless contains no structural mechanics, statics or strength-of-materials course; no fluid-mechanics or hydraulics sequence; no concrete, steel, construction-materials or foundation-design sequence; no geotechnical, traffic-engineering, road or railway-design course; and no progressive civil-engineering design studio or civil-engineering thesis. Those are core gaps across both compulsory years rather than optional specialisms. ENSSUST315 Spatial Planning is adjacent but has no offering in the six-term planning window and does not repair the engineering-sequence gap.
